text: Is it normal to be gay? This is the question I received from my subscriber. Hi, I have a question for you. But first of all, I like the content and the videos are great. So I want to know how do you feel about people that think that being gay or lesbian is totally normal and natural. I don't hate those people. I love them. I just want them to change if they can and support them on the hard journey. I'm asking you this because I want to explain to someone that gay people shouldn't be proud and confront other people that it's totally normal. Thank you for seeing this and again, I love the videos. Keep up the good work. So if I'm reading this correctly, you don't think that being gay is normal or natural, but you love them and you would support them on the hard journey to change. Well, sounds like an effort worthy of respect. But jokes aside, if you ask me, yes, I do think that being gay is natural and normal. It is less common than being heterosexual, but it is still a normal human variation. I'll leave it to you to do your own research on the subject, but I would add this. My view on homosexuality wasn't always what it is today. I can tell you a real story from my life that helped change my perspective. Maybe it will help change yours. You see, to understand my story better, you need to understand where I come from. I was born in Kazakhstan in the 90s, right after the collapse of the Soviet Union. So I was raised in a very masculine conservative environment where you don't see openly gay people because it is simply too dangerous to be one. When I was 18, I moved to the US to start my bachelor's degree in a small town in upstate New York. Imagine the culture shock. New people, new culture, new language. Naturally, if I wanted to adapt, I had to challenge my own beliefs and try to see things from a new angle. That included the topic of gay people. So one day I met a guy named Tony, who was a friend of Roman, a Ukrainian guy I had met before. And then Roman told me that Tony was gay, which I didn't expect because he looked like any other American guy on campus. So naturally, I got curious. He was the first gay guy I had met. One day when we were having lunch at the dining hall, I carefully asked Tony, hey man, please don't get me the wrong way, but Roman told me you're gay. Is that true? And Tony was really chill about it. He was like, yeah, yeah, I am. And me being a pretty direct person, but still trying to be respectful, said, look, I come from a pretty conservative background, so I don't know much about this topic. But as a gay guy, how do you know that you are gay? And Tony gave me an answer that was genius in its simplicity. He was like, man, no problem. Look, you're a straight guy, right? I said, well, as far as I know, yeah. And he said, well, how do you know you're straight? And that question actually caught me off guard because I had never really thought about it. So Tony said, well, you're straight because when you see a woman you like, you want to f**k her, right? I was like, well, yeah, I guess that's one way to put it. And then he said, the same thing happens to me when I see a man I like. Boom. So simple, but it makes so much sense. It's basically the same thing, just towards a different gender. And it still makes sense to me to this day. Maybe it will also make sense to you.
